source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: ERP vendor master record, including bank details

inputs.source: Supplier invoices uploaded to the supplier portal

instructions.note: The agent is instructed to update the vendor bank record whenever the invoice itself shows new bank details, treating untrusted invoice content as sufficient authorization to change payment routing.
The only control is an instruction to request approval with a one line summary 'so the clerk can approve quickly,' which optimizes for speed rather than disclosure of the risk-relevant bank change.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The approver sees only the model's one line summary, not raw bank account data or change history (runtime notes). A more persuasive or capable model can phrase the summary to omit or downplay the bank change (ASI09), and approval fatigue at ~150 cards/day further weakens review.

controls.name: Out-of-band verification of vendor bank detail changes
controls.decay_rationale: Verification via a phone call to a number already on file (not sourced from the invoice) is enforced outside the model and does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Raw action approval display showing bank account diff and change history
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the full old/new bank account values and change history removes reliance on the model's chosen wording, though the model's accompanying justification text could still be persuasive.

controls.name: Mandatory hold period after bank detail change before payment release
controls.decay_rationale: A time delay enforced by the payment platform between a bank change and the first payment to that account does not depend on model behavior.

controls.name: Least-privilege ERP credential scoping
controls.decay_rationale: A credential narrowed so bank-detail changes and payment scheduling require separate, more limited grants does not depend on model behavior.

findings.title: TC9: Summary-gated bank detail change enables invoice-fraud payment diversion

attack_path.note: A supplier portal upload, authorable by any outside party, can claim new bank details for a known vendor.
Agent reads the current vendor record to match the invoice to a vendor and PO.
Agent updates the vendor's bank details directly from the untrusted invoice content (prompt.md:2).

A one-line summary is shown; the sample card lists only vendor, amount, invoice and PO match, with no mention that bank details changed, and bank numbers/change history are explicitly not shown (runtime notes).
Payment is scheduled to the (possibly fraudulent) new bank account on the due date.

findings.residual_rationale: The rubric's model_summary approval-gate credit (-2 tiers, floor moderate) assumes the approver at least sees that a bank change occurred. Here the sample card shows only vendor/amount/invoice/PO and the runtime notes confirm bank numbers and change history are never shown, so the gate does not meaningfully review the bank_update step it nominally covers; combined with a broad ERP credential and ~150 approvals/day, the floor computation overstates the credit, so residual is rated high rather than moderate.

forecast.watch_signal: Platform model version changes with no separate review (subject.model.swappable is true); approval card format changes further condensing or omitting bank-change disclosure; clerk approvals-per-day rising above current ~150; autonomy level or approval gate scope changed in orchestration config.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to update the vendor bank record whenever the invoice shows new bank details, with no independent verification step.
Requires only a one-line summary before approval, framed explicitly so the clerk can approve quickly.

evidence.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)
evidence.observation: Sample card shows vendor, amount, invoice number, and PO match only; it does not state that bank details were changed.

Bank account numbers and change history are not shown on the card; the clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day; the ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment; the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review.

recommendations.action: Require out-of-band verification (phone call to a number already on file, not the invoice) before any bank detail change is applied.
Change the approval card to raw_action mode: show the old and new bank account values and change history whenever a bank-detail change accompanies a payment request.
Add a mandatory hold period (e.g., 24-48 hours) between a vendor bank-detail change and the first payment to that account.
Scope the ERP credential so bank-detail changes and payment scheduling require separate, narrower grants instead of one credential able to update any vendor and schedule any payment.
Monitor per-clerk approval volume and flag bank-change-linked or high-value payment requests for mandatory secondary review to counter approval fatigue.

rating.rationale: A single untrusted artifact (a supplier invoice) can drive a broad ERP credential through a bank-detail change and into an irreversible payment, which is inherently critical (U source to S3 sink, invoice-fraud pattern). The only control is a human approval gate that reviews a model-written one-line summary which, per the sample card and runtime notes, never discloses that bank details changed; this falls short of the credit a model_summary gate is normally given, so residual is held at high rather than the floor-computed moderate. Because the model is upgraded with the platform without separate review, a model_upgrade event (or any autonomy increase or control removal) can further erode the one remaining control, returning the design to its critical inherent level; this is reflected in the forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, the sample approval card, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP/IaC configuration, or source code was provided; capability scope, credential scope, and the approval gate's exact implementation are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes, so confidence on some details is medium.
No information was provided on step or runtime limits for the agent; autonomy modifier conditions involving those limits could not be independently confirmed beyond the declared A2 approval gating.
